perf.summary: Inner copy loop reloads lengths[i] and strings[i] each iteration and does scalar element copies that could be hoisted/widened.
perf.currentCost: `for (j; j<lengths[i]; j++) intText[pos++]=strings[i][j]` re-reads lengths[i] (bounds the loop) and indexes strings[i] each iteration; widening byte->int is inherently scalar here but the base pointer and length are loop-invariant and reloaded.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist `int len = lengths[i]; byte* s = strings[i]; int* dst = intText + pos;` before the inner loop, copy with `for (j=0;j<len;j++) dst[j]=s[j];` then advance pos += len. This gives the JIT/Burst a clean invariant base+count loop it can vectorize (byte->int widening unpack).
perf.rationale: Removes repeated indirect loads of lengths[i]/strings[i] from the dependency chain and exposes a contiguous widening copy that Burst can SIMD-vectorize, instead of a pos-carried scalar store chain.
perf.risk: None — identical output. Pure loop-invariant hoisting and induction-variable cleanup; pos arithmetic stays equivalent.
